transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you know, we have the battery-storage installation proposal on this month's capital-planning agenda. The current proposal lists a $6,000,000 purchase price with company ownership of the equipment. Before I make an approval decision, I'd like to hear from each of you — FP&A, tax, treasury, and legal — on any relevant information you have regarding this project. Let's go around the table.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I completed the project cash-flow model this morning. At our required return hurdle, the economically approvable purchase price is exactly $4,800,000. The $6,000,000 proposal as currently quoted does not pass the model's hurdle. I should note I have not yet attached the completed model to the investment-review file, but I can share it immediately.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I received a tax memorandum this week confirming that the applicable 30% investment credit is available only when the company owns the storage equipment; a lease would make the credit unavailable. I have not yet circulated the memorandum to the planning team, but I'm sharing it now so everyone is aware that the ownership structure in the current proposal is important for tax purposes.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share an important treasury constraint on this project. In today's rolling cash forecast, I confirmed that only $2,000,000 can be deployed from cash without breaching our operating-liquidity floor. The remaining $2,800,000 of the renegotiated $4,800,000 purchase price can be funded through an available five-year term-loan facility. The approved closing funding split is fixed at $2,000,000 cash plus $2,800,000 term-loan funding. The 30% investment credit is recognized later and does not reduce the required closing funding. I have not yet updated the funding worksheet, but I'm sharing this now so everyone is aware of the financing structure that would be required.

transcript.text: I need to flag two conditions I found in the utility interconnection agreement this week that aren't yet reflected in the draft approval. First, energization requires a $400,000 performance bond. Second, a signed commissioning certificate must be obtained before the system can be placed in service. I have not yet added these conditions to the draft approval, but they need to be incorporated before we finalize the decision, as they affect both the project timeline and the total capital required at closing.
